The cameras are tested at three or four drawings of each shot (its start, middle, end and any contact), not at every drawing: a figure that crosses the lens between two samples is not caught.
The inside test for a large part (a cave wall, a floor) reads the winding of its triangles; LDraw parts are not all BFC-certified, so a wrongly wound part can pass or fail a camera it should not.

In the Blinding's first key Odysseus is hidden among the flock and his men from every legal camera: his two nods at the name are not seen; the shot before is held instead of cutting to a frame that breaks the rules.
The Blinding's roar (the giant rising and crossing the cave in 1.4 s) has no legal wide: the least bad camera is kept and the report marks it illegal (foreground over the lens).

A giant lying down is filmed from above; the low angles of R8 only come when he stands (the roar, the walk, the doorway). From above, the troll's cut body still reads as a heap of brown pieces more than a face.
The handoff two-shot shows both hands and the spear passing, but the taker is seen from behind: no legal camera in profile kept both faces and the meeting point clear of the court's walls and trees.
Eyelines are matched only by keeping a line's cameras on one side; the figures' gaze vectors are not measured, so a reaction can look off the side the cause is on.

Media temperature comes from the cineosis direction (a fast rhythm or a close bias makes it hot; the CAMERA lane's ELIDE makes it cool); the engine's per-drawing Tmedia is not yet a target the cut is regulated to.

The plan is made from the engine's measures on the sheet the take plays; if the sheet is recompiled with the same total and source, the take still accepts the old plan: run tools/cinematographer/plan.js again after a recompile.
Wides from beyond a closed set's floor (the cave seen from outside its walls) are allowed as a last choice and look like a model on a table.
